editorial_reason: Read Stacks 5.11, Definitions 5.11.1 and 5.11.4. The source explicitly defines the codimension of an irreducible closed subspace and the catenary condition; it expressly does not give a codimension definition for arbitrary reducible closed sets.

definitions.text: For an irreducible closed subset Y of a topological space X, codim(Y,X) is the supremum of lengths of strict chains Y=Y_0⊊Y_1⊊⋯⊊Y_n of irreducible closed subsets of X; it may be infinite.
definitions.context_hint: Topology: codimension of an irreducible closed subset

definitions.text: A topological space X is catenary if between each pair of nested irreducible closed subsets Y⊆Z, the codimension codim(Y,Z) is finite and all maximal chains of irreducible closed subsets connecting Y to Z have the same length.
definitions.context_hint: Topology: catenary space

editorial_reason: Read Stacks Categories 4.38, Definitions 4.38.1, 4.38.2 and 4.38.3, including the equivalence with presheaves via fibre categories. These give precise distinctions between discrete categories and a category fibred in sets, as well as the associated 2-categorical morphisms.

definitions.text: A category C is discrete if every morphism in C is an identity morphism; consequently it has no arrows between distinct objects and no nonidentity endomorphisms.
definitions.context_hint: Category theory: discrete category

definitions.text: A category p:E→C is fibred in sets over C when p is a category fibred in groupoids and each fibre E_U over an object U of C is a discrete category.
definitions.context_hint: Category theory: category fibred in sets

definitions.text: For a base category C, the 2-category of categories fibred in sets over C has such fibrations as objects, functors commuting with their projections to C as 1-morphisms, and natural transformations lying over identity arrows as 2-morphisms.
definitions.context_hint: Higher category theory: 2-category of categories fibred in sets

editorial_reason: Read Stacks 10.122 introduction and Lemma 10.122.1. Quasi-finiteness of a finite-type ring map at a specified prime is characterized by the point being isolated in its fibre; it is distinct from finiteness of a ring map.

definitions.text: Let R→S be a finite-type ring homomorphism and q∈Spec(S) lying over p∈Spec(R). The map is quasi-finite at q if q is an isolated point of the fibre Spec(S⊗_R κ(p)); equivalently its local fibre has dimension zero.
definitions.context_hint: Commutative algebra: quasi-finite ring map at a prime

editorial_reason: Read Stacks 10.10 introductory description of the internal Hom module of R-linear maps and its natural module structure, including functoriality in both arguments.

definitions.text: For modules M,N over a commutative ring R, the internal Hom Hom_R(M,N) is the R-module of R-linear homomorphisms M→N, with pointwise addition and scalar multiplication (r·f)(m)=r·f(m).
definitions.context_hint: Module theory: internal Hom module of two R-modules

editorial_reason: Read Stacks 10.163 on ascending properties of rings and depth formulas. It consists of lemmas establishing how already-defined properties behave under flat maps and localizations. No separate mathematical object called an 'ascending property' is formally defined in this source section.
Read Stacks Schemes 26.3, Definitions 26.3.1 and 26.3.3. It distinguishes an open immersion of locally ringed spaces from the corresponding restricted locally ringed open subspace.

definitions.text: A morphism f:(X,O_X)→(Y,O_Y) of locally ringed spaces is an open immersion if f is a homeomorphism of X onto an open subset of Y and the induced morphism f^{-1}O_Y→O_X is an isomorphism of sheaves of rings.
definitions.context_hint: Algebraic geometry: open immersion of locally ringed spaces

definitions.text: For an open subset U of the underlying space of a locally ringed space (X,O_X), its open subspace is the locally ringed space (U,O_X|_U) obtained by restricting the structure sheaf to U.
definitions.context_hint: Algebraic geometry: open locally ringed subspace

editorial_reason: Read Stacks 10.4 Lemma 10.4.1, which constructs the snake lemma connecting morphism explicitly from a commutative diagram with exact rows. The named snake lemma is a theorem, but the canonical connecting homomorphism is a definite mathematical construction.

definitions.text: For a commutative diagram of abelian groups with exact rows X→Y→Z→0 and 0→U→V→W and vertical maps α,β,γ, the snake connecting map ∂:ker(γ)→coker(α) sends z to the class of an element u∈U whose image in V equals β(y), where y∈Y maps to z; this class is independent of the choices.
definitions.context_hint: Homological algebra: snake lemma connecting homomorphism

editorial_reason: Read Stacks 10.14 Definition 10.14.1. The source explicitly defines base change of a ring homomorphism and, separately, base change of an S-module along a map from the original base ring.

definitions.text: For ring homomorphisms R→S and R→R′, the base change of R→S along R→R′ is the induced homomorphism R′→S⊗_R R′.
definitions.context_hint: Commutative algebra: base change of a ring homomorphism

definitions.text: Given an R-algebra S, an S-module M and a map R→R′, the base change of M along R→R′ is the module M⊗_R R′ over S⊗_R R′.
definitions.context_hint: Commutative algebra: base change of a module

editorial_reason: Read Stacks 10.162 Definition 10.162.1 and its reference to N-2/Japanese domains. It distinguishes universally Japanese rings from Nagata rings, a normality finiteness property of all quotients by prime ideals.

definitions.text: A ring R is universally Japanese if every finite-type R-algebra S that is an integral domain is Japanese (N-2), meaning the integral closure of S in any finite extension of its fraction field is finite over S.
definitions.context_hint: Commutative algebra: universally Japanese ring

definitions.text: A commutative ring R is Nagata if it is Noetherian and R/p is Japanese (N-2) for each prime ideal p of R.
definitions.context_hint: Commutative algebra: Nagata ring

editorial_reason: Read Stacks 10.125 Definition 10.125.1. It explicitly defines local relative fibre dimension of a finite-type ring map at a prime of S, and the global relative dimension as their supremum.

definitions.text: For a finite-type ring map R→S and prime q of S lying over p in R, the relative dimension at q is the local topological dimension at the corresponding point of the fibre Spec(S⊗_R κ(p)).
definitions.context_hint: Commutative algebra: relative dimension of a finite-type ring map at a prime

definitions.text: The relative dimension of a finite-type ring homomorphism R→S is the supremum over all primes q∈Spec(S) of its relative fibre dimensions dim_q(S/R).
definitions.context_hint: Commutative algebra: relative dimension of a ring map

editorial_reason: Read Stacks 10.108 Definition 10.108.1 and equivalences of Lemma 10.108.2. An ideal is pure exactly when its quotient is flat, equivalently when intersection with any ideal is given by product.

definitions.text: An ideal I in a commutative ring R is pure if the quotient module R/I is flat over R.
definitions.context_hint: Commutative algebra: pure ideal

definitions.text: Equivalently, an ideal I⊆R is pure when I∩J=IJ for every ideal J of R; it is enough to test finitely generated ideals J.
definitions.context_hint: Commutative algebra: equivalent ideal-intersection criterion for purity

editorial_reason: Read Stacks 10.126, including proof of Lemma 10.126.2 which uses the finite presentation R[x_1,…,x_n]/I and finiteness of the generating relation ideal. It proves faithful-flat descent of finite presentation for both algebras and modules, so the underlying two finite-presentation notions are meaningful.

definitions.text: An R-algebra S is finitely presented if it admits a presentation S≅R[x_1,…,x_n]/(f_1,…,f_m) with finitely many generators x_i and finitely many polynomial relations f_j.
definitions.context_hint: Commutative algebra: algebra of finite presentation

definitions.text: An R-module M is finitely presented if an exact sequence R^m→R^n→M→0 exists with both m and n finite; equivalently M has finitely many generators and relations.
definitions.context_hint: Module theory: finitely presented module
